newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Invesco takes fine, says no client lost.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Invesco takes fine, says no client lost.

text.p: British investments watchdog IMRO said on Thursday it had fined Invesco Asset Management 60,000 pounds sterling ($97,400) for breaches of its rules on dealing with client money.
Invesco said it had reported the infractions to IMRO as soon as they came to light and that none of its clients had lost any money.
"We obviously regret this happened but we found it and immediately reported it to the regulator," Tristan Hillgarth, chief executive of Invesco Europe told Reuters.

The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation said in a statement that Invesco, which is now part of investment management group Amvesco Plc (soon to be renamed AMVESCAP), would also have to pay costs of 25,500 pounds, after agreeing to settle disciplinary proceedings against it.

IMRO said Invesco, which merged with AIM Management Group Inc, had failed to reconcile client money bank accounts on time, failed to correct differences on reconciliations and failed to maintain written compliance procedures.
This is the third time that Invesco has fallen foul of the watchdog but Hillgarth said the latest breach of the rules was completely unrelated to earlier incidents.

In 1991, Invesco MIM Management was fined 75,000 pounds for failings in dealing with Personal Equity Plan (PEP) administration and client money, affecting 110,000 people and 220 million pounds of investments.

This investigation led to a much larger 750,000 pounds fine and over 1.5 million pounds of costs in June 1993, when Invesco MIM, Invesco MIM Unit Trust Managers and Invesco Ventures faced 55 charges relating to widespread management and procedural failings.
Invesco Asset management has around 5.5 billion pounds under management for institutional and retail customers, including around 80,000 PEP investors.
